items.label: Student: "Can you help with my final-year project?"
Head of Ops at a 200-person clinic chain: "Need a patient booking app, budget approved, want to start next month"
Startup founder: "Building an AI tutoring MVP, have funding, can we talk this week?"

task.explanation: Prioritise by fit and readiness: approved budget and timeline first, then a funded founder; a student project is off-ICP and vendor pitches are not leads.

segments.text: Contact form submitted Monday 10:05 with a detailed project brief.

segments.issue: Days of delay lets the lead cool and contact competitors; reply within hours.

segments.text: Reply thanked them and asked two questions about their timeline and users.
Lead was not logged in the CRM because "it's in my inbox".
segments.issue: Unlogged leads have no source attribution and get lost if the rep is away.

segments.text: A calendar link was offered to book a call.
Lead source recorded as "Website - contact form" after the call.

prompt: A Friday evening enquiry reads: "We run 30 gyms and want a member app with class booking and payments. Who can I talk to?"

task.prompt: A Friday evening enquiry reads: "We run 30 gyms and want a member app with class booking and payments. Who can I talk to?"

steps.question: What is the best first response?
options: Wait until Monday's team meeting to decide who owns it
Send a quick personal reply acknowledging the brief with a booking link for early next week
Send a generic auto-reply only
Send a full proposal tonight
steps.explanation: A fast, personal acknowledgement with an easy next step holds the lead's attention.

steps.question: They book a call. What should you prepare?
options: A fixed price quote
A contract
Nothing, it's discovery
Research their brand, existing app or website, and two relevant examples; draft a few discovery questions
steps.explanation: Light research and relevant proof make the first call useful for the buyer.

steps.question: After the call, the lead is qualified. What updates the CRM?
options: Only their email address
Source, company, contact role, needs, budget/timeline signals and the dated next step
Nothing until they sign
A note saying "good call"
steps.explanation: A complete record lets anyone pick up the deal and keeps source reporting accurate.

prompt: Order the inbound lead handling process.

task.prompt: Order the inbound lead handling process.

items.label: Qualify fit and book a discovery call
Run discovery and send a recap
Move to proposal or politely disqualify
Enquiry arrives and is routed to an owner
Owner replies quickly and logs the lead with its source

task.explanation: Route, respond and log, qualify, discover, then decide — each step depends on the one before.

prompt: Why is lead response time so important for inbound enquiries?

options: Interest is highest right after enquiring and the buyer is often contacting several agencies
It is a legal requirement
Slow replies lower the project price
Search engines rank fast responders higher
mcq.explanation: Buyers shortlist whoever engages first and well; delay hands the conversation to a competitor.

prompt: What is the main reason to record the lead source for every inbound lead in the CRM?

options: To fill in a mandatory field
To send the lead a newsletter
To calculate the project estimate
To know which channels actually produce revenue and where to invest
mcq.explanation: Source attribution shows which channels convert, guiding marketing spend and effort.

prompt: Inbound volume doubled but won deals stayed flat. What should you check first?

options: How many emails reps send per day
The office location
Whether the new leads match the ICP and how qualification is going
The website's colour scheme
mcq.explanation: More leads that do not fit, or that are qualified poorly, raise volume without raising wins.
